title: Phase 2 — proposing and accepting
blurb: The proposer has heard back and now proposes a value; acceptors accept it. This is where the protocol is won or lost.

payload.describe: Acceptor 1 accepts Alice in ballot 1.

justification.text: Paxos does not allow this step: Acceptor 1 has promised ballot 2, so it will not accept in the lower ballot 1 — that promise is exactly a commitment to ignore anything older. An acceptor accepts in a ballot only if that ballot is the same as, or higher than, the highest ballot it has promised. The same as matters: the normal path through the protocol is an acceptor promising a ballot and then accepting in that very ballot.

payload.describe: Acceptor 1 accepts Alice in ballot 2.

justification.text: Paxos allows this step — there must be a proposal to accept; the ballot must be at least as high as the promise. When an acceptor accepts a value in some ballot, it records that ballot as both its promised ballot and the ballot of its last acceptance, records the value, and announces it so everyone can see.

payload.describe: The proposer running ballot 2, after hearing back from Acceptor 1 and Acceptor 3, proposes Bob.

justification.text: Paxos allows this step — a ballot may carry at most one proposal; a majority must have promised this ballot; propose the value reported from the highest ballot. A proposal says which ballot it belongs to and which value is being put forward.

payload.describe: The proposer running ballot 2, after hearing back from Acceptor 1 and Acceptor 3, proposes Alice.

justification.text: Paxos does not allow this step: the highest acceptance reported to this proposer is Bob in ballot 1, from Acceptor 1. That forces the proposer to propose Bob, not Alice. If any acceptor in the majority reported something it had already accepted, the proposer is not free to choose. It must propose the value that was reported together with the highest ballot number among those reports. This single rule is what makes Paxos safe: it is how a value that may already have been agreed on gets carried forward into every later attempt.

payload.describe: The proposer running ballot 0, after hearing back from Acceptor 1 and Acceptor 3, proposes Bob.

justification.text: Paxos does not allow this step: ballot 0 already carries a proposal of Alice, and a ballot carries at most one. A proposer makes at most one proposal per ballot. If two different values could be proposed under the same ballot number, two different values could both be accepted by a majority at that ballot, and the acceptors would have agreed on two things at once.
